title: Frame
description: Positions at one frame, in pitch metres. The ground-truth data and the tracker output share this shape so eval can diff them. Rendered frames add the optional image-space labels (camera, boxes, visibility, keypoints); pixel coordinates have their origin at the top-left image corner, and pixel (i, j) covers [i, i+1] x [j, j+1].

frame.description: Match frame index at 25 fps; event.frame refers to the same index.

clip.description: Rendered frames: id of the clip this frame belongs to.

image.description: Rendered frames: image path relative to the clip directory.

pixels.description: Pixels the ball covers in the image when drawn alone.

center_px.description: Ball centre projected through the camera.

centroid_px.description: Centroid of the ball's drawn pixels.

heading.description: Radians in the pitch plane (0 = toward x=105): the way the player faces, which turns his body (ninety/sim/shape.py).

camera.description: Rendered frames: the exact pinhole camera. P = K [R | t] maps homogeneous pitch metres (x, y, z, 1) to pixels.

blur_px.description: Rendered frames: motion-blur streak from the camera pan, in pixels.

keypoints.description: Rendered frames: named pitch points that fall inside the image. visible is false when a player, the goal frame or the scorebug covers the point.

bbox.description: [x0, y0, x1, y1] in pixels around everything drawn of the object inside the image, occluded parts included; null when none of it is drawn.

visibility.description: Share of the object's in-image pixels not hidden by other players, the ball, the goal frame, the scenery (boards, stands, roofs, towers) or the scorebug, counted by the renderer. 0 with a bbox means in shot and fully hidden.
